summary:
ORBITAL ARCHITECT is a browser-based 3D space mission engineering game modeled after NASA JPL’s Mission Design Lab (MDL) and General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT). Players act as mission architects to plan, assemble, launch, and operate complete space missions across progressive destinations from Low Earth Orbit to the Moon, Mars, and Europa.   

Space mission engineering is typically taught through isolated theoretical exercises, leaving students disconnected from how real spacecraft subsystems interact. ORBITAL ARCHITECT bridges this gap through a coupled systems-engineering engine and real-time 3D WebGL visualizer. Every component choice triggers authentic trade-offs: heavier instruments demand larger launch vehicles, outer-planet distances reduce solar flux via the inverse-square law, planetary eclipses drain battery reserves, and high-rate sensors require high-gain Deep Space Network antennas.   

Featuring Solo, 4-Player Team Sync, Sandbox, and Custom Architect modes—alongside interactive mid-flight solar storm decisions, root-cause engineering audits, and real NASA flight-heritage comparisons—the game turns complex systems engineering into an accessible, hands-on experience for students, educators, and aspiring aerospace engineers.
details:
ORBITAL ARCHITECT

3D SPACE MISSION ENGINEERING SIMULATION GAME

ORBITAL ARCHITECT is a browser-based 3D space mission engineering game inspired by NASA JPL’s Mission Design Lab (MDL) and General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT).

Rather than teaching orbital mechanics, rocket propulsion, and spacecraft subsystems as isolated textbook concepts, the game puts players in the role of mission architects. Players must design, balance, launch, and operate a complete space mission, progressing from initial mission planning to orbital operations.

1. Mission Briefing & Mode Selection

Players begin by selecting a game mode and choosing a mission contract.

Available Game Modes:

  • Solo Architect: Design and operate missions independently.
  • 4-Player Team Sync: Collaborate with three other players to complete a mission.
  • Sandbox Lab: Experiment freely with spacecraft configurations and mission parameters.
  • Custom Architect Mode: Create missions with customizable objectives and constraints.

2. Four-Step Interactive Assembly Hangar

Players configure their spacecraft through four interactive engineering stages:

  1. Launch Vehicle & Orbit: Select the launch vehicle, configure payload capacity, and determine the target orbit.
  2. Scientific Instruments: Choose scientific payloads based on mission objectives and data-generation requirements.
  3. Power & Thermal Systems: Configure solar panels, batteries, nuclear power sources, and thermal management systems.
  4. Deep Space Network (DSN) Communications: Select communication bands and antennas to establish reliable spacecraft-to-ground communication.

Real-Time Coupled Physics Engine

The physics.js engine continuously evaluates spacecraft configurations and calculates the consequences of engineering decisions.

Core Engineering Simulations:

- Mass vs. Booster Capacity: Calculates the combined mass of the spacecraft bus, scientific instruments, power systems, and communication antennas against the launch vehicle's payload capacity.

- Inverse-Square Solar Flux (\(1/r^2\)): Dynamically calculates available solar energy based on the spacecraft's distance from the Sun. Solar power decreases from 100% at Earth and the Moon to approximately 43% at Mars (1.52 AU) and 3.7% at Europa (5.2 AU), making nuclear MMRTG power sources essential for outer-planet missions.

- Orbital Eclipse Survival: Simulates battery discharge during planetary shadow passages and determines whether the spacecraft can maintain essential operations without sunlight.

- RF Downlink Bandwidth: Compares the total scientific instrument data-generation rate (Mbps) against S-Band, X-Band, and Ka-Band communication capacities to prevent data overflow.

3. 3D Launch & Accelerated Orbital Flight Simulation

Once spacecraft assembly is complete, players initiate the launch sequence with a T-3 countdown, transitioning into a real-time 3D orbital simulation.

Powered by scene3d.js, the visualizer features:

  • Planetary Shadow Cones: Visual representations of planetary shadows and orbital eclipse conditions.
  • Surface Target Zones: Interactive mission destinations and designated observation regions.
  • DSN Telemetry Beams: Live cyan communication beams representing spacecraft-to-ground data transmission.
  • Accelerated Orbital Flight: Experience mission progression without waiting for actual orbital durations.
  • Interactive Mid-Flight Anomalies: Encounter unexpected events, such as a Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) solar storm, that require immediate engineering decisions.

Players must act as flight directors, making real-time trade-offs to protect spacecraft systems, preserve mission objectives, and maintain operational stability.

4. Post-Flight Engineering Audit

At mission completion, the game generates a comprehensive engineering performance report.

Mission Evaluation Includes:

  • Final Mission Rank: A performance grade ranging from S to FAILED.
  • Root-Cause Engineering Breakdown: Identifies the exact engineering decisions responsible for mission successes, inefficiencies, and failures.
  • Subsystem Performance Analysis: Evaluates spacecraft mass, power availability, thermal stability, orbital survival, and communication efficiency.
  • Mission Heritage Comparison: Compares the player's spacecraft design and mission outcomes against real NASA flight-heritage missions.

5. Benefits & Intended Impact

Bridging the Systems-Engineering Gap

Traditional educational tools often teach orbital trajectories, rocket launches, and spacecraft subsystems as separate concepts. ORBITAL ARCHITECT bridges this gap by demonstrating how spacecraft subsystems interact and compete for limited resources, including mass, power, budget, and data transmission capacity.

Students experience the engineering trade-offs involved in designing a spacecraft, understanding that there is no universally perfect design—only designs optimized for specific mission objectives and constraints.

Accessible Across Skill Levels

The game incorporates beginner-friendly learning features without compromising the authenticity of its aerospace engineering concepts.

  • Flight Director Onboarding: A guided 3-step introduction familiarizes new players with mission planning and spacecraft operations.
  • Plain-English Engineering Callouts: Explains engineering trade-offs and their consequences in an understandable manner.
  • One-Click Starter Blueprints: The Load Baseline feature provides ready-made spacecraft configurations that players can modify and improve.
  • Smart Launch-Blocker Hints: Identifies configuration problems and provides actionable guidance before launch.

These features make the experience accessible to middle and high school students while retaining meaningful engineering challenges for aspiring aerospace engineers.

Zero-Barrier Classroom & Workshop Deployment

ORBITAL ARCHITECT operates entirely within a standard web browser, requiring no software installation or backend server infrastructure.

This makes it suitable for:

  • School and college classrooms.
  • STEM education programs and aerospace outreach clubs.
  • Hackathons and engineering workshops.
  • Collaborative mission-design challenges.
  • Self-guided learning on laptops and Chromebooks.

Its lightweight deployment model allows educators and participants to start designing missions without complicated setup procedures.

6. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

Programming Languages

  • HTML5: Provides the application structure and interface.
  • CSS3: Handles styling, responsive layouts, animations, and the JPL-inspired telemetry aesthetic.
  • JavaScript (ES6+): Implements the application logic through modular architecture, including physics.js, scene3d.js, and app.js.

3D Graphics & Visualization

Celestrak Visualizer | Noelkawano

Three.js (WebGL)

Powers procedural 3D spacecraft assembly, structural over-mass wireframe alerts, three-point studio and solar lighting, orbital trajectory splines, and planetary eclipse shadow geometry.

Retro Futuristic Satellite Control Center Interface Display

HTML5 2D Canvas

Renders tactical radar sweeps, telemetry oscilloscopes, and floating real-time statistical popups.

Audio & User Interface

  • Web Audio API: Generates procedural NASA-style Quindar tones, telemetry clicks, and launch rumble effects without relying on external audio files.
  • Google Fonts: Uses Inter and JetBrains Mono for a modern, technical interface.
  • Material Symbols Outlined: Provides consistent icons throughout the application.

7. Creativity & Key Design Considerations

Custom Architect Mode for Educators & Engineers

Unlike fixed-scenario simulations, Custom Architect Mode provides extensive mission customization capabilities.

Users can:

  • Define custom mission budgets and scientific targets.
  • Adjust solar flux percentages to simulate different mission environments.
  • Edit the $M cost of existing spacecraft subsystems directly.
  • Create entirely new hardware components across all four assembly stages.
  • Dynamically integrate custom components into the 3D spacecraft model.

This transforms the application from a predefined game into a flexible mission-design environment suitable for experimentation, education, and engineering demonstrations.


Lightweight 4-Player Team Collaboration

The Team Sync system enables up to four players to collaborate using Base64-encoded configuration tokens.

Each participant can take responsibility for a different engineering discipline:

  1. Flight Director: Oversees mission objectives, launch readiness, and overall mission decisions.
  2. Payload Lead: Manages scientific instruments, payload mass, and data-generation requirements.
  3. Power Engineer: Handles electrical power generation, battery capacity, and thermal considerations.
  4. Communications Officer: Manages antennas, communication bands, and downlink bandwidth.

Each teammate operates from a separate console, contributing to the overall spacecraft configuration without requiring an external database or backend infrastructure.
